headline: Hard Fork and AI Daily Brief treat Huang as out at Nvidia; still no company filing

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's quarter to three UTC on Friday, November thirteenth. This is ARA AI News. The AI Daily Brief now says Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia, and Hard Fork has a matching downfall episode.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The AI Daily Brief posted a twenty-nine minute episode titled Jensen Huang is out, and says everything in AI is now up for grabs.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That is a shift. Earlier this morning we noted that the same show had listed spy-scandal fallout and had not said Huang resigned.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Hard Fork now has a thirty-eight minute episode framed as the downfall of the most powerful man in AI. That is the show that first put the Times-cited affair and Megaspeed claims on this board.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: We still have only titles and runtimes. Neither episode has a transcript in this hour, and Nvidia has not issued a statement, a filing, or a named successor.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Decoder remains the first show that said Huang resigned, in an intro it said it rewrote minutes before publishing, as the affair reports and the alleged Chinese-spy claims threatened to take over the company.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Hard Fork and the Daily Brief are now treating that Decoder claim as the live fact in their episode titles. That is media confirmation beyond Decoder, not a company confirmation.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The Daily Brief's line that everything in AI is now up for grabs is the show's own framing of a vacuum at the top of Nvidia. It is not a company plan, and we should not read it as one.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The underlying allegations have not moved. Hard Fork had already described a Malaysia preferred-cloud partner in twenty twenty-three, and said if ten or fifteen percent of Nvidia's revenue was coming from Malaysia those chips were being distributed to China.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Last night on twenty VC, guests said hosting inference and G P U chips for China-based models in Singapore and Thailand will get shut down, and that a House bill had already stalled in the Senate.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Watch next for the spoken reporting on those two episodes. A board statement that names a successor, or any Nvidia filing, is still the hard fact this story does not have.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Until that lands, the picture is a Decoder resignation claim now echoed by Hard Fork and the Daily Brief, sitting on top of the spy and export allegations, with no first-party confirmation.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
